claim: A standard buffer of 50 mM bis TRIS-propane pH 6.5, 300 mM NaCl, 5% glycerol was chosen for comparing activity of full-length SpNOX to SpNOXDH.
source: Thus, for all experiments in which we compare activity of the full-length SpNOX to the truncated SpNOXDH, we chose a standard buffer of 50 mM bis TRIS-propane pH 6.5, 300 mM NaCl, 5% glycerol.
evidence: This is a methodological decision based on optimization experiments.

claim: SpNOXDH requires supplemental FAD to sustain both superoxide production and NADPH oxidation.
source: Like purified or membrane preparations of both the full-length and DH constructs of other NOX family members (Han et al., 2001; Nisimoto et al., 2004; Nisimoto et al., 2010), SpNOXDH requires supplemental FAD to sustain both superoxide production, which can be observed in the presence of Cyt c (Figure 3A), and NADPH oxidation, which can be observed in the absence of Cyt c (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by activity assay data shown in Figure 3A and 3B, and by citation to similar observations in other NOX family members.

claim: The dependence of SpNOXDH on flavin in the oxidation of NADPH was confirmed by inhibition with diphenyleneiodonium (DPI).
source: The dependence of SpNOXDH on flavin in the oxidation of NADPH was assessed by addition of diphenyleneiodonium (DPI), a common specific flavoenzyme inhibitor (Nisimoto et al., 2014), which inhibited the enzyme activity (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by DPI inhibition data shown in Figure 3C and citation to DPI as a flavoenzyme inhibitor.

claim: The addition of superoxide dismutase (SOD) led to a ~40% inhibition of SpNOXDH's Cyt. c reductase activity.
source: The addition of superoxide dismutase (SOD) led to a ~40% inhibition of SpNOXDH's Cyt. c reductase activity, confirming that the reduction of Cyt. c observed in the system is partly due to O2●- generation (Figure 3D and Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3D and Table 1.

claim: The reduction of Cyt. c by SpNOXDH is partly due to O2●- generation.
source: The addition of superoxide dismutase (SOD) led to a ~40% inhibition of SpNOXDH's Cyt. c reductase activity, confirming that the reduction of Cyt. c observed in the system is partly due to O2●- generation (Figure 3D and Table 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the partial inhibition by SOD, which specifically removes superoxide.

claim: The remaining ~60% Cyt. c reductase activity of SpNOXDH after SOD addition suggests direct electron transfer from FADH2 to Cyt. c.
source: However, the remaining~60%Cyt. c reductase activity suggests direct electron transfer from the FADH2 produced by the SpNOXDH to the Cyt. c.
evidence: This is inferred from the SOD-insensitive portion of Cyt. c reduction.

claim: SpNOXDH retained the redox properties and sensitivity displayed in the context of the whole SpNOX protein (Hajjar et al., 2017).
source: Thus, SpNOXDH, separated from the TM domain, retained the redox properties and sensitivity displayed in the context of the whole SpNOX protein (Hajjar et al., 2017).
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the properties of SpNOXDH with those previously reported for full-length SpNOX.

claim: The strict requirement of FAD addition for SpNOXDH activity and its µM level of affinity suggests that the flavin behaves as a co-substrate rather than a prosthetic group.
source: The strict requirement of FAD addition for SpNOXDH activity and its µM level of affinity suggests that the flavin behaves as a co-substrate rather than a prosthetic group.
evidence: This is inferred from the requirement for exogenous FAD and the measured Km values.

claim: As an isolated domain, SpNOXDH may work as a flavin reductase enzyme (Gaudu et al., 1994; Fieschi et al., 1995; Nivière et al., 1996).
source: As an isolated domain, SpNOXDH may work as a flavin reductase enzyme (Gaudu et al., 1994; Fieschi et al., 1995; Nivière et al., 1996), making an interesting parallel with the E. coli flavin reductase fre (also in the FNR family) which reduces the MsrQ transmembrane component (in the FRD family, like the NOX TM domain, see Figure 7; Caux et al., 2021; Juillan-Binard et al., 2017).
evidence: This is speculated based on the properties of SpNOXDH and comparison with other flavin reductases, supported by citations.

claim: SpNOX shows a 263-fold higher affinity for FAD than for lumiflavin.
source: We observed a progressive loss of affinity for SpNOX as flavin size diminishes, with 263-fold higher affinity for FAD than for lumiflavin (Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by Km measurements shown in Table 2.

claim: SpNOXDH retains constant affinity equal to that of lumiflavin (~10 μM) regardless of the flavin analog.
source: In contrast, the SpNOXDH retains constant affinity equal to that of lumiflavin (~10 μM) regardless of the flavin analog.
evidence: This is supported by Km measurements shown in Table 2.

claim: The isolated DH domain binds to FAD primarily at the isoalloxazine ring of the cofactor.
source: These results suggest that the isolated DH domain binds to FAD primarily at the isoalloxazine ring of the cofactor, and the addition of ribitol (riboflavin), phosphate groups (FMN), and adenosine nucleotide (FAD) do not further interact significantly with the isolated DH domain.
evidence: This is inferred from the similar Km values for all flavin analogs in SpNOXDH.

claim: The full-length SpNOX appears to interact along the entire length of the FAD cofactor.
source: However, the full-length SpNOX appears to interact along the entire length of the FAD cofactor, indicating significant interactions between the FAD and the TM domain.
evidence: This is inferred from the progressive increase in affinity with larger flavin analogs in full-length SpNOX.

claim: The FAD binding site is shared between the TM and DH domains.
source: This FAD binding site shared between the TM and DH domains may contribute to the correct placement of the cofactor for electron transfer to the proximal heme.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential flavin binding properties of full-length vs DH-only constructs.

claim: In full-length SpNOX, the kcat appears to be independent of the flavin derivative used.
source: On the other hand, in full-length SpNOX the kcat appears to be independent of the flavin derivative used, suggesting that the binding interactions between TM and FAD play no catalytic role and that only the isoalloxazine ring needs to be taken into account for the electron pathway from NADPH to the first heme.
evidence: This is supported by kcat measurements shown in Table 2.

claim: The binding interactions between TM and FAD play no catalytic role.
source: On the other hand, in full-length SpNOX the kcat appears to be independent of the flavin derivative used, suggesting that the binding interactions between TM and FAD play no catalytic role and that only the isoalloxazine ring needs to be taken into account for the electron pathway from NADPH to the first heme.
evidence: This is inferred from the independence of kcat on flavin size.

claim: Only the isoalloxazine ring needs to be taken into account for the electron pathway from NADPH to the first heme.
source: On the other hand, in full-length SpNOX the kcat appears to be independent of the flavin derivative used, suggesting that the binding interactions between TM and FAD play no catalytic role and that only the isoalloxazine ring needs to be taken into account for the electron pathway from NADPH to the first heme.
evidence: This is inferred from the kcat data showing no dependence on flavin size.

claim: The kcat of full-length and DH-only constructs are the same order of magnitude, with ratios around 1.
source: Finally, the kcat of full-length and DH-only constructs are the same order of magnitude, with ratios around 1 (Table 2), showing that the presence (or absence) of the hemes in the TM domain has little effect on the rate.

claim: The presence or absence of the hemes in the TM domain has little effect on the rate of electron transfer.
source: Finally, the kcat of full-length and DH-only constructs are the same order of magnitude, with ratios around 1 (Table 2), showing that the presence (or absence) of the hemes in the TM domain has little effect on the rate.
evidence: This is inferred from the similar kcat values of full-length and DH-only constructs.

claim: The reduction of FAD – that is, hydride transfer from the nicotinamide – is the rate limiting step in the electron transfer from substrate to O2.
source: It follows that the reduction of FAD – that is, hydride transfer from the nicotinamide – is the rate limiting step in the electron transfer from substrate to O2.
evidence: This is inferred from the similar kcat values regardless of the presence of hemes.

claim: Full length and DH constructs showed the same order of magnitude affinity to each other for NADPH or NADH as substrate.
source: Full length and DH constructs showed the same order of magnitude affinity to each other for NADPH or NADH as substrate (Table 3).
evidence: This is supported by Km measurements shown in Table 3.

claim: SpNOX does not discriminate significantly between NADPH and NADH.
source: Furthermore, the value of 1 for NADPH/NADH affinity for each construct shows that SpNOX does not discriminate significantly between NADPH and NADH; the agreement of two different assays – cytochrome c reduction and NADPH oxidation – strengthens this observation.
evidence: This is supported by Km measurements showing similar values for NADPH and NADH in Table 3.

claim: The NAD(P)H binding energy in SpNOX arises from interactions just in the DH domain with little contribution from the TM domain.
source: Thus, in SpNOX, the NAD(P)H binding energy arises from interactions just in the DH domain with little contribution from the TM domain of SpNOX.
evidence: This is inferred from the similar Km values for NAD(P)H in full-length and DH-only constructs.

claim: The lack of discrimination of SpNOX between NADH and NADPH represents a significant difference from eukaryotic NOX which strongly select NADPH as substrate.
source: The lack of discrimination of SpNOX between NADH and NADPH represents a significant difference from eukaryotic NOX which strongly select NADPH as substrate.
evidence: This is based on comparison with established knowledge about eukaryotic NOX substrate specificity.

claim: Large hexagonal crystals of SpNOX were obtained but with poor diffraction power beyond 5 Å.
source: We obtained large hexagonal crystals of SpNOX but with poor diffraction power beyond 5 Å, and only 6% between 3 and 5 Å, with clear anisotropy.
evidence: This is based on crystallographic data collection experience.

claim: The FNR C-terminal Y308 stabilizes the isoalloxazine site of the FAD cofactor and regulates access of the NADP+ substrate to this site (Deng et al., 1999).
source: We therefore tried stabilizing mutations based on the work of Deng et al., 1999 in pea FNR, homologous to the NOX DH domain. They showed that the FNR C-terminal Y308 stabilizes the isoalloxazine site of the FAD cofactor and regulates access of the NADP + substrate to this site; other works extended the discussion of the importance of this residue to the NOX DH domain (Zhen et al., 1998; Kean et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work on FNR.

claim: Magnani et al reported the stabilizing effect in CsNOX of the serendipitous insertion of a Trp that stacks with the FAD isoalloxazine ring (Ceccon et al., 2017; Magnani et al., 2017).
source: Supporting this approach, Magnani et al reported the stabilizing effect in CsNOX of the serendipitous insertion of a Trp that stacks with the FAD isoalloxazine ring (Ceccon et al., 2017; Magnani et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous structural work.

claim: F399W mutants of SpNOXDH showed normal activity.
source: We mutated both positions to tryptophan in the SpNOXDH construct and monitored activity to test their effects. In our standard buffer used for comparing DH with full-length constructs, F399W mutants showed normal activity (Table 3), while F397W mutants showed no activity (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by activity data shown in Table 3.

claim: F397W mutants of SpNOXDH showed no activity.
source: We mutated both positions to tryptophan in the SpNOXDH construct and monitored activity to test their effects. In our standard buffer used for comparing DH with full-length constructs, F399W mutants showed normal activity (Table 3), while F397W mutants showed no activity (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by activity data shown in Figure 4.

claim: W in position 397 prevents hydride transfer by immobile stacking with the isoalloxazine ring of FAD.
source: We interpreted this to mean that W in position 397 prevents hydride transfer by immobile stacking with the isoalloxazine ring of FAD, while W in position 399 has little effect on hydride transfer.
evidence: This is inferred from the loss of activity in F397W mutants and structural considerations.

claim: W in position 399 has little effect on hydride transfer.
source: We interpreted this to mean that W in position 397 prevents hydride transfer by immobile stacking with the isoalloxazine ring of FAD, while W in position 399 has little effect on hydride transfer.
evidence: This is inferred from the normal activity of F399W mutants.

claim: F397 of SpNOX corresponds to the terminal Y of FNR.
source: These results indicate that F397 of SpNOX corresponds to the terminal Y of FNR.
evidence: This is inferred from the functional effects of mutations at position 397.

claim: The flavin content of purified F397W is much higher than that of WT.
source: The flavin content of purified F397W is much higher than that of WT, while the F397S is not able to retain flavin in its binding site (Figure 4A), consistent with our hypothesis about flavin binding.
evidence: This is supported by UV-visible spectroscopy data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: F397S is not able to retain flavin in its binding site.
source: The flavin content of purified F397W is much higher than that of WT, while the F397S is not able to retain flavin in its binding site (Figure 4A), consistent with our hypothesis about flavin binding.
evidence: This is supported by UV-visible spectroscopy data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: F397W has little or no activity in standard activity conditions.
source: As displayed in Figure 4B, in our standard activity conditions, F397W has little or no activity while F397S shows enhanced activity compared to WT.
evidence: This is supported by activity assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: F397S shows enhanced activity compared to WT.
source: As displayed in Figure 4B, in our standard activity conditions, F397W has little or no activity while F397S shows enhanced activity compared to WT.
evidence: This is supported by activity assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Increasing the NADPH concentration 10-fold resulted in low but significant activity of the F397W mutant.
source: Increasing the NADPH concentration 10-fold resulted in low but significant activity of the F397W mutant (not shown).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations not shown in figures.

claim: The W and S mutations of position 397 do not significantly affect the structural integrity of the SpNOX constructs.
source: These results indicate that the W and S mutations of position 397 do not significantly affect the structural integrity of the SpNOX constructs.
evidence: This is inferred from the ability to purify and characterize these mutants.

claim: F397S mutants show similar Km values to WT for both NADPH and NADH in both full-length enzyme and DH constructs.
source: F397S mutants show similar results to WT (Table 3) in both constructs indicating that S in this position does not greatly impact affinity for either substrate; this mutation produced an increase in kcat for both constructs, consistent with the hypothesis that S in this position provides increased access of substrate to the catalytic site.
evidence: This is supported by kinetic data shown in Table 3.

claim: F397S mutation produced an increase in kcat for both full-length and DH constructs.
source: F397S mutants show similar results to WT (Table 3) in both constructs indicating that S in this position does not greatly impact affinity for either substrate; this mutation produced an increase in kcat for both constructs, consistent with the hypothesis that S in this position provides increased access of substrate to the catalytic site.
evidence: This is supported by kinetic data shown in Table 3.

claim: S in position 397 provides increased access of substrate to the catalytic site.
source: F397S mutants show similar results to WT (Table 3) in both constructs indicating that S in this position does not greatly impact affinity for either substrate; this mutation produced an increase in kcat for both constructs, consistent with the hypothesis that S in this position provides increased access of substrate to the catalytic site.
evidence: This is inferred from the increased kcat in F397S mutants.

claim: The use of the full-length SpNOX F397W construct resulted in about 20% of the crystals displaying diffraction limits close to 4 Å.
source: The use of the full-length SpNOX F397W construct resulted in about 20% of the crystals produced displaying diffraction limits close to 4 Å, with some crystals showing an anisotropic diffraction between 3 and 3.3 Å in a privileged direction of the crystals, as often observed for membrane proteins (Martin et al., 2023; Robert et al., 2017).
evidence: This is based on crystallographic data collection experience.

claim: Some crystals of full-length SpNOX F397W showed anisotropic diffraction between 3 and 3.3 Å in a privileged direction.
source: The use of the full-length SpNOX F397W construct resulted in about 20% of the crystals produced displaying diffraction limits close to 4 Å, with some crystals showing an anisotropic diffraction between 3 and 3.3 Å in a privileged direction of the crystals, as often observed for membrane proteins (Martin et al., 2023; Robert et al., 2017).
evidence: This is based on crystallographic data collection experience, with citation to similar observations in membrane proteins.

claim: De novo resolution at 1.94 Å of SpNOXDH F397W was achieved using bromide-SAD.
source: De novo resolution at 1.94 Å of SpNOXDH F397W was possible because we co-crystallized in the presence of sodium bromide and collected a bromide-SAD dataset (see methods).
evidence: This is based on the crystallographic methods and results described.

claim: The SpNOXDH WT structure was solved at 2.5 Å resolution using the SpNOXDH F397W structure as a model.
source: To solve the SpNOXDH WT structure, we used the SpNOXDH F397W structure as a model, and achieved 2.5 Å resolution.
evidence: This is based on the crystallographic methods and results described.

claim: SpNOXDH presents a typical fold of the FNR superfamily of reductase domain containing two sub-domains, the FAD-binding domain (FBD) and an NADPH-binding domain (NBD).
source: As expected, SpNOXDH presents a typical fold of the FNR superfamily of reductase domain containing two sub-domains, the FAD-binding domain (FBD) and an NADPH-binding domain (NBD) (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by the crystal structure shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Both WT and F397W SpNOXDH display 3 molecules per asymmetric unit and the two structures are identical.
source: Both WT and F397W SpNOXDH display 3 molecules per asymmetric unit and the two structures are identical.
evidence: This is based on crystallographic analysis.

claim: In the asymmetric unit of SpNOXDH WT, one of the three molecules contains no flavin.
source: In the asymmetric unit of SpNOXDH WT, one of the three molecules contains no flavin (Figure 5—figure supplement 2.).
evidence: This is based on crystallographic analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: In the asymmetric unit of SpNOXDH F397W, all molecules contain a well-defined FAD.
source: In the asymmetric unit of SpNOXDH F397W, all molecules of the unit contain a well-defined FAD (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on crystallographic analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The crystallographic observations agree with flavin contents observed in solution.
source: These observations agree with flavin contents observed in solution (Figure 4A) and support the hypothesis that the F397W mutant stabilizes FAD binding.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing crystallographic and solution data.

claim: The F397W mutant stabilizes FAD binding.
source: These observations agree with flavin contents observed in solution (Figure 4A) and support the hypothesis that the F397W mutant stabilizes FAD binding.
evidence: This is inferred from the higher flavin content and complete FAD occupancy in F397W structures.

claim: The DH domain mainly interacts with the isoalloxazine ring through polar contacts with the protein backbone and a few residues (P234, F235, and S23) belonging to the conserved FAD-1 binding motif (Massari et al., 2022).
source: In strong correlation with the affinity data obtained for the flavins shown in Table 2, the DH domain mainly interacts with the isoalloxazine ring through polar contacts with the protein backbone and a few residues (P234, F235, and S23) belonging to the conserved FAD-1 binding motif (Massari et al., 2022; see Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 5D and correlation with affinity data in Table 2.

claim: The DH domain shows almost no contact with the ribitol and adenosine parts of the FAD.
source: The DH domain shows almost no contact with the ribitol and adenosine parts of the FAD.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the FAD binding site.

claim: The rest of the FAD molecule points out into the solvent, in the direction of the missing TM domain.
source: With the exception of possible polar contact of the first phosphate group with the backbone of the protein, the rest of the FAD molecule points out into the solvent, in the direction of the missing TM domain (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: In the wild type SpNOXDH, the isoalloxazine ring is sandwiched between FBD residues P234 and F235 on its si-face, and the NBD residue F397 on its re-face.
source: In the wild type, the isoalloxazine ring is sandwiched between FBD residues P234 and F235 on its si-face, and the NBD residue F397 on its re-face (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: In SpNOXDH WT, the F397 aromatic ring imperfectly occupies the position in front of the re-face of the isoalloxazine ring, with orientation 40° with respect to the plane of the isoalloxazine ring, and distance at 5.3 Å.
source: Superposition of the different SpNOXDH WT molecules from the crystal asymmetric unit shows that the F397 aromatic ring imperfectly occupies the position in front of the re-face of the isoalloxazine ring (Figure 5B), with orientation 40° with respect to the plane of the isoalloxazine ring, and distance at 5.3 Å.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The tryptophan of the F397W mutation makes an extensive and much tighter parallel stacking interaction at a distance of 3.5 Å from the isoalloxazine ring.
source: In contrast (and as predicted from the homologous FNR structure), the tryptophan of the F397W mutation makes an extensive and much tighter parallel stacking interaction at a distance of 3.5 Å from the isoalloxazine ring (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: WT SpNOXDH could behave as a flavin reductase, able to use different flavins as substrate through the sole recognition of the isoalloxazine ring.
source: From these observations, WT SpNOXDH could well behave as a flavin reductase, able to use different flavins as substrate through the sole recognition of the isoalloxazine ring.
evidence: This is inferred from structural observations and affinity data.

claim: The F397W mutant may fix the flavin as a cofactor.
source: As Figure 4A shows, the F397W mutant may fix the flavin as a cofactor.
evidence: This is inferred from the high flavin content in F397W shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Trp at position 397 appears to preclude access of the nicotinamide to the isoalloxazine, preventing direct hydride transfer.
source: Trp at position 397 appears to preclude access of the nicotinamide to the isoalloxazine, preventing direct hydride transfer.
evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis shown in Figure 5E and the lack of activity in F397W.

claim: Phe in position 397 leaves more space in the active site pocket and the sidechain has more degrees of freedom, making it feasible for the nicotinamide to displace it and transfer hydride to the isoalloxazine.
source: Phe in this position, however, leaves more space in this pocket and the sidechain has more degrees of freedom, making it feasible for the nicotinamide to displace it and transfer hydride to the isoalloxazine.
evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis and comparison with F397W.

claim: The structural observations explain the drastic difference of activity between WT and F397W.
source: These observations most likely explain the drastic difference of activity between WT and F397W; they probably also explain the enhanced activity observed in the F397S mutant which provides even more space near the isoalloxazine (Table 3).

claim: The F397S mutant provides even more space near the isoalloxazine.
source: These observations most likely explain the drastic difference of activity between WT and F397W; they probably also explain the enhanced activity observed in the F397S mutant which provides even more space near the isoalloxazine (Table 3).
evidence: This is inferred from the smaller size of serine compared to phenylalanine.

claim: The increase of the global kcat in the F397S mutant is an additional argument to support hydride transfer as the limiting step in NOX electron transfer.
source: The increase of the global kcat in the F397S mutant is an additional argument to support hydride transfer as the limiting step in NOX electron transfer.
evidence: This is inferred from the kinetic data showing increased kcat in F397S.

claim: The high-resolution model of the DH domain of SpNOX allowed resolution of the anisotropic crystals of full-length SpNOX-F397W to 3.6 Å.
source: The high-resolution model of the DH domain of SpNOX allowed resolution of the anisotropic crystals of full-length SpNOX-F397W to 3.6 Å.
evidence: This is based on the crystallographic methods used.

claim: Small extracellular loops limiting crystal contacts together with intrinsic interdomain flexibility of SpNOX are probably the source of the crystal anisotropy.
source: Small extracellular loops limiting crystal contacts together with intrinsic interdomain flexibility of SpNOX are probably the source of the crystal anisotropy due to subtle variation of packing within the crystals (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is speculated based on structural analysis and common issues in membrane protein crystallography.

claim: The crystallographic model of SpNOX harbors the N-terminal TM domain that encompasses 6 membrane-spanning alpha helices chelating two hemes, and the C-terminal cytosolic DH domain.
source: Like the previously reported structures of the NOX family (Liu et al., 2022; Magnani et al., 2017; Sun, 2020; Wu et al., 2021), the crystallographic model of SpNOX harbors the N-terminal TM domain that encompasses 6 membrane-spanning alpha helices chelating two hemes, and the C-terminal cytosolic DH domain (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is based on the crystal structure shown in Figure 6A and comparison with other NOX structures.

claim: The inner and outer heme are respectively coordinated by the imidazole rings of pairs of histidines H69 (TM3)/H129 (TM5) and H82 (TM3)/H142 (TM5), holding them perpendicular to the plane of the membrane (Vermot et al., 2020).
source: The inner and outer heme are respectively coordinated by the imidazole rings of pairs of histidines H69 (TM3)/H129 (TM5) and H82 (TM3)/H142 (TM5), holding them perpendicular to the plane of the membrane (Vermot et al., 2020).
